title: Behavioral & HR for Python Freshers
intro: Behavioral and HR interview questions take up 30–50% of every fresher Python interview — not because the interviewer has run out of technical questions, but because at 0 YOE, your communication skills and attitude matter as much as your code. This page covers the questions that come up in almost every fresher round: the self-introduction (the four-part formula: education → project → skill highlight → why this company, in under 90 seconds), 'why Python?' (the answer that shows genuine interest, not 'because it's easy' which always lands badly), explaining a college project (how to frame it as a problem-solution-result story, not a feature list), strength and weakness (the framework for a genuine weakness that doesn't disqualify you), team conflict (the STAR answer structure for a disagree-and-commit story), career goals (realistic 3-year framing for a fresher), and the follow-up questions that come after every technical answer ('what would you do differently?' and 'how did you learn that?'). Every answer is written for a 22–24-year-old first-job interview, not a senior engineering manager behavioural.
